message.content: /unattended:interview I want a small script that counts the words in the text files in ./notes and writes the twenty most common words to a CSV. I keep runs in ./run/ and this run's folder is ./run/2026-11-12-word-counter/. I only want the brief, do not start the work.

content.text:
Before I search or draft anything, three questions, each with my proposed answer:

1. What it is for. Proposal: so you can see which words you lean on in your notes.
2. What counts as a word. Proposal: any run of letters between spaces or punctuation, lowercased, so "The" and "the" are one word.
3. What the CSV holds. Proposal: two columns, word and count, most common first, written to ./notes/top_words.csv.

message.content: 1 yes. 2 also drop words of one letter. 3 yes, but put it in ./out/top_words.csv instead, I don't want to touch ./notes.

content.text:
Thanks, those are settled and written down in the rulings file. Last batch before I attack the brief, four things, each with my proposed answer:

1. How we will know it works. Proposal: run `python count_words.py ./notes` on three small test files whose counts you can check by hand; the CSV matches your hand counts exactly, ties broken alphabetically.
2. If it fails. Proposal: if the script still miscounts after three honest attempts, stop and report the files and the counts that differ; do not loosen the rule for what counts as a word.
3. What the run may touch. Proposal: it may create and edit files only in ./out and its own run folder, and may run python and the test command; it may not delete or overwrite anything in ./notes.
4. The budget.
Budget: I'll keep it to a reasonable share of your quota.
